title: The Rehearsal
hook: He erased part of this room.
caption:
He erased part of this room.

Degas's The Rehearsal (c. 1873–78) hangs at Harvard. Look close and you'll find a lone violinist shoved into the corner, the 'petits rats' of the Paris Opéra at the barre, and a ghost: Harvard says Degas later painted out a whole stairwell. In his Glasgow version, that spiral stair survives, dancers' legs coming down it, cut off by the frame.

He wasn't backstage when he painted this. His dancers came to his studio to pose. And the men who were backstage? That's slide 5.

Swipe to the end, then watch the reel: we flew a camera straight into the room. Save this for your next museum visit.

slides.headline: The Rehearsal — Edgar Degas, c. 1873–78

slides.headline: No backstage pass. So they came to him.

notes: IMPORTANT: assets/degas/degas_rehearsal_fogg_full.jpg is the Harvard/Fogg painting (1951.47, 47.2 x 61.5 cm; aspect matches). assets/sources/degas_rehearsal_1878_2000.jpg is a DIFFERENT work: the Frick Collection's The Rehearsal (1878–79), bearded violinist foreground — not used. Several suggested angles (spiral staircase with legs, ballet master/Perrot, woman adjusting a dress) belong to the Burrell Collection (Glasgow) version, c. 1874, not the Fogg one; the Fogg canvas has no staircase, ballet master or dresser. Harvard's own text says Degas later reworked the Fogg picture, removing a stairwell — so the staircase became the twist, illustrated with the Glasgow version. Harvard images: museum permits noncommercial/educational use; the painting scan is our own asset. Unverified Degas 'ashamed' letter quote deliberately not used.
